send keyed messages to kafka
produce key-value pairs to the user-events topic

kafka-produce-with-headers.name: Produce messages with headers
kafka-produce-with-headers.description: Produces messages with custom headers to a Kafka topic. Headers are key-value metadata attached to messages without being part of the message payload. Useful for routing, tracing, and metadata propagation.

examples.query: produce messages with headers to the events topic
send messages with custom headers in kafka
publish data with tracing headers

kafka-produce-with-serializer.name: Produce with specific serializer
kafka-produce-with-serializer.description: Produces messages using a specific serializer class for the value. Common serializers include StringSerializer, IntegerSerializer, and custom Avro or JSON serializers. The key serializer can also be set via key.serializer.

examples.query: produce messages using a custom serializer
send avro serialized messages to kafka

kafka-consume-messages.name: Consume messages from a topic
kafka-consume-messages.description: Starts a console consumer that reads and displays messages from the specified Kafka topic. By default, it only consumes new messages arriving after the consumer starts. Press Ctrl+C to stop consuming.

examples.query: consume messages from the orders topic
read messages from kafka topic events
listen to messages on user-activity topic

kafka-consume-from-beginning.name: Consume from beginning
kafka-consume-from-beginning.description: Consumes all messages from the beginning of the topic. This reads every message stored in the topic from the earliest available offset across all partitions.

examples.query: consume all messages from the beginning of the orders topic
read the entire topic from the start
replay all messages in the events topic

kafka-consume-from-offset.name: Consume from specific offset
kafka-consume-from-offset.description: Consumes messages from a specific partition starting at a specific offset. This allows precise control over which messages to read. The offset is a zero-based index of the message within the partition.

examples.query: consume from partition 0 starting at offset 100
read messages from offset 500 in partition 2

kafka-consume-with-key.name: Consume messages with key
kafka-consume-with-key.description: Consumes messages and displays both the key and value for each message. The key and value are separated by the specified separator character in the output. Useful for debugging keyed messages.

examples.query: consume messages showing keys from the orders topic

kafka-consume-with-headers.name: Consume messages with headers
kafka-consume-with-headers.description: Consumes messages and displays the headers attached to each message. Headers contain metadata key-value pairs that were set by the producer. Useful for tracing and debugging message flow.

examples.query: consume messages showing headers from the orders topic
display message headers from kafka
read messages with their header metadata

kafka-consume-with-timestamp.name: Consume messages with timestamps
kafka-consume-with-timestamp.description: Consumes messages and displays the timestamp of each message. The timestamp can be either the creation time (set by the producer) or the log append time (set by the broker), depending on the topic's message.timestamp.type configuration.

examples.query: consume messages showing timestamps
read messages with their timestamps
display when each message was produced

kafka-consume-with-deserializer.name: Consume with specific deserializer
kafka-consume-with-deserializer.description: Consumes messages using a specific deserializer class for the value. Common deserializers include StringDeserializer, IntegerDeserializer, and custom Avro or JSON deserializers. The key deserializer can also be set via key.deserializer.

examples.query: consume messages using a custom deserializer
read avro deserialized messages from kafka
consume with string deserializer from topic

kafka-list-consumer-groups.name: List consumer groups
kafka-list-consumer-groups.description: Lists all consumer groups registered with the Kafka cluster. This includes both active and inactive consumer groups. Useful for discovering which applications are consuming from the cluster.

examples.query: list all consumer groups
show me the consumer groups on the cluster
what consumer groups are active

kafka-describe-consumer-group.name: Describe consumer group
kafka-describe-consumer-group.description: Describes a consumer group showing detailed information including the current offset, log end offset, and lag for each partition assigned to the group. Also shows the consumer ID, host, and client ID of each group member.

examples.query: describe the consumer group my-app-group
show lag for consumer group order-processor
check offsets of the consumer group
what is the lag for my consumer group

kafka-consumer-group-members.name: List consumer group members
kafka-consumer-group-members.description: Lists the members of a consumer group including their consumer IDs, host addresses, client IDs, and the number of partitions assigned to each member. Useful for checking consumer distribution and balance.

examples.query: list members of consumer group my-app-group
show who is consuming in the group

kafka-consumer-group-lag.name: Check consumer lag
kafka-consumer-group-lag.description: Checks the consumer lag for a consumer group with verbose output. Shows the current offset, log end offset, and lag for each topic-partition assigned to the group. High lag indicates consumers are falling behind.

examples.query: check the lag for consumer group order-processor

kafka-delete-consumer-group.name: Delete consumer group
kafka-delete-consumer-group.description: Deletes a consumer group and all its committed offsets. The consumer group must have no active members (all consumers must be stopped). This operation is irreversible.

examples.query: delete the consumer group old-processor
remove the inactive consumer group
clean up the unused consumer group

kafka-reset-offsets-to-earliest.name: Reset offsets to earliest
kafka-reset-offsets-to-earliest.description: Resets consumer group offsets to the earliest available offset for the specified topic. This causes the consumer group to re-consume all available messages from the beginning. The consumer group must be inactive.

examples.query: reset offsets to earliest for group my-app on topic orders
rewind consumer group to the beginning
replay all messages for the consumer group

kafka-reset-offsets-to-latest.name: Reset offsets to latest
kafka-reset-offsets-to-latest.description: Resets consumer group offsets to the latest offset for the specified topic. This causes the consumer group to skip all existing messages and only consume new messages going forward. The consumer group must be inactive.

examples.query: reset offsets to latest for group my-app on topic orders
skip to the end of the topic for the consumer group
jump to the latest offset

kafka-reset-offsets-to-timestamp.name: Reset offsets to timestamp
kafka-reset-offsets-to-timestamp.description: Resets consumer group offsets to the offset corresponding to the given timestamp. Messages produced after this timestamp will be reconsumed. The timestamp format is ISO 8601. The consumer group must be inactive.

examples.query: reset offsets to 2026-01-15T10:00:00.000 for the consumer group
rewind consumer to messages from yesterday

kafka-reset-offsets-to-offset.name: Reset offsets to specific offset
kafka-reset-offsets-to-offset.description: Resets consumer group offsets to a specific offset value for the specified topic. This sets the same offset for all partitions of the topic. The consumer group must be inactive.

examples.query: reset offsets to offset 1000 for group my-app
set the consumer group offset to 500
move consumer to a specific offset

kafka-reset-offsets-by-duration.name: Reset offsets by duration
kafka-reset-offsets-by-duration.description: Resets consumer group offsets by subtracting the specified duration from the current time. Uses ISO 8601 duration format (e.g., PT1H for 1 hour, P1D for 1 day, PT30M for 30 minutes). The consumer group must be inactive.

examples.query: reset offsets by 2 hours for the consumer group
rewind the consumer group by 1 day
replay the last 30 minutes of messages

kafka-describe-topic-config.name: Describe topic configuration
kafka-describe-topic-config.description: Describes all configuration overrides for a specific topic. Shows only the configs that differ from the broker defaults. Useful for auditing topic-level settings like retention, cleanup policy, and compression.

examples.query: describe the configuration of topic orders
what are the config overrides for the events topic

kafka-alter-topic-config.name: Alter topic configuration
kafka-alter-topic-config.description: Modifies a configuration property for a specific topic. Common configs include retention.ms, cleanup.policy, max.message.bytes, compression.type, and segment.bytes. Multiple configs can be set by comma-separating them.

examples.query: set retention to 7 days for the orders topic
change the cleanup policy to compact for topic user-profiles

kafka-describe-broker-config.name: Describe broker configuration
kafka-describe-broker-config.description: Describes the dynamic configuration overrides for a specific broker. Shows only the configs that have been dynamically changed from the static broker defaults. Use --entity-default for cluster-wide defaults.

examples.query: describe the configuration of broker 0
show dynamic config for broker 1
what are the broker configuration overrides

kafka-alter-broker-config.name: Alter broker configuration
kafka-alter-broker-config.description: Dynamically modifies a configuration property for a specific broker without requiring a restart. Common dynamic configs include log.retention.ms, log.retention.bytes, and num.io.threads. Not all broker configs can be changed dynamically.

examples.query: change the log retention on broker 0
dynamically update broker configuration
set a broker config without restart

kafka-describe-cluster.name: Describe cluster
kafka-describe-cluster.description: Describes the Kafka cluster metadata including cluster ID, controller, and broker information. For KRaft-based clusters, use kafka-metadata.sh. Alternatively, kafka-broker-api-versions.sh can show broker API versions.

examples.query: describe the kafka cluster
show me the cluster metadata
what is the cluster ID

kafka-list-acls.name: List ACLs
kafka-list-acls.description: Lists all Access Control Lists (ACLs) configured in the Kafka cluster. Shows which principals have which permissions on which resources (topics, groups, cluster, transactional IDs).

examples.query: list all ACLs in the cluster
show me the kafka access control lists
what permissions are configured

kafka-add-acl.name: Add ACL
kafka-add-acl.description: Adds an Access Control List (ACL) entry to allow a principal to perform a specific operation on a resource. Common operations include Read, Write, Create, Delete, Alter, Describe, and All.

examples.query: grant read access on topic orders to user app-consumer
add write permission for user producer-app on topic events
allow user admin to read from all topics

kafka-remove-acl.name: Remove ACL
kafka-remove-acl.description: Removes an Access Control List (ACL) entry, revoking a principal's permission to perform the specified operation on the resource. Use with caution as it may break applications that depend on the permission.

examples.query: remove read access on topic orders from user old-consumer

kafka-reassign-partitions-generate.name: Generate partition reassignment plan
kafka-reassign-partitions-generate.description: Generates a partition reassignment plan for moving topic partitions to the specified brokers. Outputs the current assignment and a proposed new assignment. The topics JSON file should contain a list of topics to move in the format {"topics":[{"topic":"t1"}],"version":1}.

examples.query: generate a partition reassignment plan for brokers 0,1,2

kafka-reassign-partitions-execute.name: Execute partition reassignment
kafka-reassign-partitions-execute.description: Executes a partition reassignment plan, moving partitions to the brokers specified in the reassignment JSON file. This triggers data replication across brokers and may impact cluster performance during the process.

examples.query: execute the partition reassignment plan

kafka-reassign-partitions-verify.name: Verify partition reassignment
kafka-reassign-partitions-verify.description: Verifies the status of a partition reassignment. Shows whether the reassignment is still in progress, completed successfully, or failed. Should be run after executing a reassignment to confirm completion.

examples.query: verify the partition reassignment status

kafka-describe-log-dirs.name: Describe log directories

kafka-dump-log.name: Inspect log segments
kafka-dump-log.description: Inspects Kafka log segment files on disk, displaying the contents of messages stored in the segment. Useful for low-level debugging and forensic analysis of message data. The --print-data-log flag shows the actual message payloads.

examples.query: inspect the kafka log segment file

read raw messages from a kafka log file

kafka-describe-topic-config-all.name: Describe all topic configs
kafka-describe-topic-config-all.description: Describes all configuration properties for a topic, including both overridden values and default values inherited from broker configuration. The --all flag shows every config property and its source.

kafka-delete-topic-config.name: Delete topic configuration override
kafka-delete-topic-config.description: Removes a configuration override from a topic, reverting it to the broker default value. Useful for cleaning up custom topic configurations that are no longer needed.

kafka-create-topic-with-config.name: Create topic with custom configuration
kafka-create-topic-with-config.description: Creates a new Kafka topic with custom configuration properties set at creation time. Multiple --config flags can be used to set several properties. Common configs include retention.ms, cleanup.policy, compression.type, and max.message.bytes.

kafka-consume-with-group.name: Consume with consumer group
kafka-consume-with-group.description: Consumes messages from a topic as part of a specific consumer group. Offsets are committed automatically for the group, enabling resumption from where the consumer left off. Multiple consumers with the same group ID share the partitions.
